situation.text: Hoje você conhece Andre, de Columbus. Pechinchar em venda de garagem.

pages.goal: Hoje você aprende a fechar um acordo: It’s a deal! e Deal! (combinado!).

pages.hook: In many American towns, people sell old things from their garage or yard on a weekend morning. You can ask the price, make an offer and often pay less than the sign says.
pages.polite: Be friendly: **How much is this?**, **Can you do eight?**, **Thanks for stopping by!**

mythfact.s: A garage sale is where people sell used things from home.
mythfact.why: Families sell old chairs, books, toys and more.

mythfact.s: At a garage sale, asking for a lower price is often normal.
mythfact.why: Many sellers expect an offer, such as “Can you do eight?”

mythfact.s: Garage sales happen only inside big stores.
mythfact.why: They usually happen in a garage, yard or driveway.

mythfact.s: Garage sales are often on weekends.
mythfact.why: Many people have more free time on Saturday or Sunday.

mythfact.s: You must always pay the price on the sticker.
mythfact.why: Often you can make a small offer.

decode.q: How much are the lamp and the toy car together?

compare.br: In Brazil people also sell used things at a “bazar” or a “brechó”, and asking for a discount is common.
compare.us: In the USA a garage sale is often at someone’s house, and many sellers happily say “OK, eight dollars.”
compare.tip: Make the offer friendly: “Can you do eight?” and smile.
compare.ask: Have you ever bought something used? Say what it was in English.

pages.title: Cultural spotlight
Reading quest — A deal on Saturday
text: Brad lives in **Columbus**. On Saturday morning, he puts a sign on the street: “**Garage sale**.” He has a lamp, a chair, some books and a toy. He wants a **fair price** for each thing.

Andre comes at nine. He sees the lamp. “Hi! **How much is this lamp?**” he asks. “Ten dollars,” says Brad. “**Can you do eight?**” Andre asks. Brad thinks. “OK, eight dollars.” Andre smiles. They both feel good.

Then Andre looks at the chair. “And this chair?” “Fifteen. **It’s in good shape**,” says Brad. Andre says, “I’ll take both for twenty.” Brad says, “**Sounds good! It’s a deal!**” They **shake on it**. The word “deal” means “agreement”. Andre pays with twenty dollars.

Brad likes the day. At home that night, he watches “**Shark Tank**”, an American TV show that started in 2009. People ask rich investors for money, and sometimes they **strike a deal**. Brad laughs: “My garage sale is a very small deal, but I like it.”
The sale ends at noon. Brad has twenty-eight dollars, a clean garage and a happy afternoon. “**Thanks for stopping by!**” he says to the last visitor. “See you next time!”
